prompt: Answers keep stopping mid-sentence even though the model clearly had more to say.
why: The response hit its max-token limit; raise it.
trap: A content filter would block, not cut cleanly at a length.

prompt: Finance wants every reply capped so no single answer can run up a large bill.
why: Max tokens bounds output length, and output tokens are billed.
trap: A smaller model is cheaper per token but doesn't cap length.

prompt: Replies are sent by text message and must stay short.
why: A low max-token limit enforces brevity.
trap: The system prompt can ask for brevity, but max tokens guarantees a ceiling.

prompt: A 600-word answer is cut off although the limit was set to 600. A colleague assumed the limit counted words.
why: The limit counts tokens, and English averages about 3/4 of a word per token, so 600 tokens is roughly 450 words.
trap: The limit is fine as a concept; the unit is tokens.

prompt: A model returns long JSON objects, and some arrive with the closing braces missing so they fail to parse.
why: Cut-off output is the max-token limit; raise it or ask for shorter output.
trap: Examples can't fix a hard length cap.

prompt: A long document plus the prompt nearly fills the model's context window, leaving room for only a few hundred tokens of answer.
tells: leaving room for only a few hundred tokens of answer
why: Input and output share the context window, so the room left for the answer caps its length.
trap: A different deployment type doesn't enlarge the context window.

prompt: A chatbot sometimes writes 2,000-word replies to simple questions, slowing the app and raising costs.
why: A max-token cap stops runaway replies.
trap: A smaller model writes just as long if allowed.

prompt: Summaries must fit in a 160-character notification. The prompt asks for brevity, but some run long.
why: A hard max-token limit guarantees an upper bound.
trap: A prompt asks; the limit enforces.
